Keyboard shortcuts

Press ? anywhere in Soleil Clusters to see the shortcut list without leaving the page. The essentials are V to select, H or Space to pan, N for a note, A for an arrow, Cmd-K to search everything, Cmd-Z to undo, and Shift-1 to fit the whole board on screen.

Updated October 24, 2026

Press ? on any canvas to see this list in the app, where it shows the right modifier key for your platform. On Windows and Linux, every ⌘ below is Ctrl.

Tools

KeyAction
VSelect / move
H or SpacePan the canvas
NAdd a note
DFree-draw — unless W A S D movement is on
AArrow — unless W A S D movement is on
GAdd a grid
CAdd a cluster — click where it goes
EscBack to select · close whatever is on top — a menu, a dialog, Settings

Navigate

KeyAction
⌘K or /Search and commands
⌘BToggle sidebar
⌘.Clean mode — hide all chrome
↑ / ↓ in a right-click menuMove through it — → opens a submenu and ← closes it, Enter chooses

⌘K is the fastest way to get anywhere. It searches cluster names, card contents, notes, docs and tags, and it also runs commands — "share", "trash", "theme", "invite" all work as typed input.

Sidebar

In the sidebar: its cluster tree and its Files. Tab reaches the rows; these act on the focused one.

KeyAction
Enter or SpaceOpen the cluster
→ / ←Expand · collapse the clusters inside it
F2Rename the cluster — Enter saves, Esc cancels
⇧F10 or MenuThe row's menu — the same one right-click opens
↑ / ↓Move through the clusters, or through the files
SpaceQuick look at the focused file
EnterGo to the focused file — on its board, or in Files when it isn't on the board
← / →On the Files tabs: the cluster, Recent, Starred. ↓ on the cluster's tab lists the other clusters
⌘\Hide · show Files — outside a note or a doc, where it clears formatting
⌥ while dragging filesCopy them instead of moving them — Ctrl (or Alt) on Windows

Edit

KeyAction
⌘Z / ⌘⇧ZUndo · redo
⌘C / ⌘X / ⌘VCopy · cut · paste
⌘DDuplicate
⌘ASelect all
⌘GGroup selection
[ / ]Send backward · forward
⌫ or DelDelete selection
Undo is per-session and per-board. It undoes your own edits, not a collaborator's — in a shared board, undo that could revert someone else's work would be worse than no undo at all.

View

KeyAction
FOpen or close the full Files page
⌘IInfo — the selection, or the cluster when nothing is selected
⌘0Reset zoom
⌘+ / ⌘−Zoom in · out
⇧1Fit everything
⇧2Fit selection
Space-dragPan with any tool active
W A S DMove around the board, ⇧ for faster — once you turn it on
Q / EZoom in · out around the middle of the screen, ⇧ for faster — with W A S D movement on
ScrollPan the canvas — or zoom, if you swap it
⌘-scrollZoom at the pointer

Zoom and pan are remembered per cluster. Reopening a board puts you back where you were rather than at the origin.

Swapping what the wheel does

Settings → Appearance → Scroll wheel. Scrolling pans by default and ⌘-scroll zooms; set it to Zoom and they trade places, so a plain scroll zooms at the pointer and ⌘, Alt or Shift pans. ⌘K → "scroll wheel" flips it without opening settings.

Which one is right depends on what you came from — PureRef and Miro zoom on scroll, Figma and Milanote pan — which is why it is a setting and not a default we picked for you.

Pinching a trackpad zooms in either mode, and always will: a pinch reaches the browser as a Ctrl-scroll, so Ctrl means zoom whatever else is configured.

Moving with W A S D

Settings → Appearance → Move with W A S D. Off until you turn it on. Then hold W, A, S or D to move up, left, down or right — two at once go diagonally — and hold Q to zoom in or E to zoom out, around the middle of the screen. Add ⇧ to go faster at either, or move and zoom at once. Letting go eases to a stop.

It is off by default because two of those keys already have a job: A picks the Arrow tool and D picks Free-draw. While movement is on they move you instead, and both tools stay one click away on the tool rail. ⌘A and ⌘D (select all, duplicate) work as before.

It goes by where the keys sit rather than the letters printed on them, so on an AZERTY keyboard it is Z, Q, S and D to move and A and E to zoom, and the same two tools give way. Like the rest of Appearance, the setting follows your account to every device.

Files

On the full Files page.

KeyAction
TabInto the folders — one stop each, where Enter opens it and Space selects it — then the files, as a single stop
← → ↑ ↓Move through files — in the grid, ↑ / ↓ go to the nearest tile in the next row
EnterSelect the highlighted file
⇧SpaceAdd the highlighted file to the selection, or take it out — the keyboard version of a tile's round check
Space or double-clickQuick look — ← / → step through the files, Space or Esc closes
⌘IInfo for the selection, or the cluster — in full-screen Files, remembered on your device
F2Rename the selected file or folder — Enter saves, Esc cancels
⇧F10The right-click menu, for the selection
⌘ASelect every file showing — search and filters apply
EscClear the selection
⌫ or DelDelete the selection, with undo
⌘Z / ⌘⇧ZUndo · redo

Audio

KeyAction
EnterPlay · pause the selected clip
LLoop the selected clip
SpaceAudition the highlighted row (Files, list layout)

Enter rather than Space on the canvas, because Space is already the pan modifier there. In Files it isn't, so auditioning a pack is ↓ and Space — and when a clip finishes, the next one starts on its own.

Both canvas keys only fire when exactly one audio card is selected; otherwise they fall through to whatever else is listening.

Player

While the review player is open, it has the keyboard — nothing reaches the board behind it. Press ? in the player for this list.

Transport

KeyAction
SpacePlay · pause
J / K / LPlay backward · stop · forward — again to go faster
K+J / K+LTap: one frame back · forward. Hold: play slowly
← / →One frame back · forward
, / .One frame back · forward
⇧← / ⇧→One second back · forward
Home / EndFirst · last frame
⇧< / ⇧>Slower · faster
0–9Type a timecode, frame or seconds to jump to

Marking

KeyAction
I / OSet in · out
⇧I / ⇧OGo to in · out
⇧SpacePlay from in to out
⌥LLoop (between in and out, or the whole clip)
⌥XClear in and out

View

KeyAction
⌥= / ⌥−Zoom the timeline in · out
⌥0Fit the whole clip in the timeline
⇧ZZoom the timeline to in and out
ZZoom the picture: fit · 100% · 200% — drag to look around
GFraming guides — again for the next one
FFull screen
MMute
⇧↑ / ⇧↓Volume up · down

Review

KeyAction
\Flip to the version you compare with
⌘CCopy the timecode
⇧⌘CCopy a link to this frame
?Show these shortcuts
EscClose the player

Notes

KeyAction
Double-clickEdit a note or a title
⌘Z / ⌘⇧ZUndo · redo text — history survives closing the note
⌘B / ⌘I / ⌘UBold · italic · underline
⌘\Clear formatting — links and comments stay
@Mention a board, doc, or card

Document

These apply inside a document, not on the canvas.

KeyAction
⌘Z / ⌘⇧ZUndo · redo — text while typing; pages & structure otherwise
⌘⌥1 / ⌘⌥0Heading 1 · body
⌘⇧7 / ⌘⇧8 / ⌘⇧9Numbered · bullet · task list
⌘⇧H / ⌘EHighlight · inline code
⌘\Clear formatting — links and comments stay
⌘⇧L / ⌘⇧E / ⌘⇧RAlign left · center · right
⌘K / ⌘⌥MLink · comment
⌘FFind and replace, in the side panel, across every page
⌘= / ⌘− / ⌘0Zoom in · out · back to 100% — a screenplay too wide for its space goes back to fitting it
EscClose a full-screen document, when you aren't typing in it

Toolbars

Every toolbar is one Tab stop, and the arrow keys move inside it: the tool rail, the bar a note, a drawing or a shape brings up, a document's toolbar, and the bar over selected files.

KeyAction
TabTo the next toolbar — each is one stop
⌥F10 / EscFrom a document's or a note's text to its toolbar · back to the text — Alt+F10 on Windows; in a table, to the table's bar
← / →The previous · next control in it — ↑ / ↓ on the tool rail
Home / EndIts first · last control
→ / ←Open · close the tool rail's + menu

In a document or a note, Tab belongs to the text (it indents), so ⌥F10 is the way from the words to the toolbar, and Esc takes you back with the caret where you left it. In a field inside a toolbar, like a font size, ← and → move the caret, and step out of the field at either end. A screen reader hears each control by its name, whether a toggle is on, and the shortcut it has, if any.

Gestures

Not keys, but worth knowing:

  • Double-click empty canvas opens an add menu at your cursor.
  • Right-click anything for its full menu — cards, groups, and the canvas background each have their own.
  • Hold Alt while dragging to bypass snapping.
  • Hold ⌥ while dragging files to another cluster to copy them instead of moving them — Ctrl on Windows.
  • Paste a URL onto the canvas to create a link card that unfurls its preview.
  • Drag files from your desktop straight onto the canvas.

Frequently asked questions

How do I see shortcuts without leaving what I am doing?

Press ? on any canvas, or click the help button in the corner of the canvas. The overlay lists every shortcut grouped by what it affects.

Can the scroll wheel zoom instead of scrolling the board around?

Yes. Settings → Appearance → Scroll wheel, or Cmd-K and type "scroll wheel". Scrolling pans by default and Cmd-scroll zooms; switching to Zoom trades them over. Pinching a trackpad zooms either way.

Can I move around a board with W, A, S and D?

Yes, once you turn it on in Settings → Appearance → Move with W A S D. Hold a key to move that way, hold Q or E to zoom in or out, and add Shift to go faster. It is off by default because A and D also pick the Arrow and Free-draw tools, which they stop doing while it is on.

Do these work on Windows?

Yes. Every Cmd shortcut listed here is Ctrl on Windows and Linux. The in-app overlay detects your platform and shows the right modifier.
